description:
FOUND s499j (probed perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at 5145fb1c, before the must-win marker was added to lib/Carp.pm).  Reproducer: `mkdir -p d && cp "$(perl -MCarp -e 'print $INC{"Carp.pm"}')" d/ && PERL5LIB=d pcl -e 'use Carp; eval { croak "boom" }; print $@'` -- perl prints `boom at -e line 1.`; PCL printed `Undefined subroutine &main::croak called at (eval 0) line 0.`  So the real Carp.pm transpiles and loads but its export of croak into the importer never happens.

WHY IT MATTERS: Carp is dual-life, and a local::lib PERL5LIB often carries a newer Carp.pm; task #2462 (s499j) put PERL5LIB AHEAD of PCL's lib/ (perl's order), so without a by-name exception every such program would break.  s499j therefore marked lib/Carp.pm `# pcl-shim: must-win` (it wins by name over @INC order, like the XS shims) -- that is the workaround, and its header says why.

WHEN THIS CLOSES: find why perl's Carp.pm leaves croak undefined in the importer (its import is Exporter's, with an export_fail hook), fix the mechanism, then consider dropping the must-win marker from lib/Carp.pm (perl's order would then let a user's Carp win, as in perl).  Probe: the command above, with the marker removed from lib/Carp.pm.
subject: perl's REAL Carp.pm does not run under PCL: loaded from PERL5LIB/-I, `use Carp; croak "x"` dies "Undefined subroutine &main::croak" (the lib/Carp.pm shim is must-win because of it)
